templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. Some [B] are [C].
3. All [C] are [D].
4. No [D] are [E].
Conclusion I: Some [B] are [D].
Conclusion II: No [C] are [E].
Conclusion III: Some [A] are [D] is a possibility.
Conclusion IV: No [B] are [E].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: Some B are C + All C are D → Some B are D (I valid). All C are D + No D are E → No C are E (II valid). III is a possibility. Some B are D + No D are E → Some B are not E (IV says No B are E which is too strong — not valid). I, II and III follow.

4. Some [E] are not [D].
Conclusion I: All [A] are [D].
Conclusion II: Some [E] are not [A].
Conclusion III: Some [E] are not [B].
Conclusion IV: Some [E] are not [C].
Which all follow?
templates.explanation: All A→B→C→D (I valid). Some E are not D → since all A/B/C are D, those E not in D are also not in A, not in B, not in C. So II, III, IV all valid. All four follow.

Conclusion III: No [A] are [D].

templates.explanation: No A are B + All B→C→D. Does No A are B mean No A are C? Not necessarily (A may be C through other means). So I and III are NOT necessarily valid. Some E are A + No A are B → Some E are not B (II valid). We cannot conclude Some E are not C from these. Only II definitely follows.
